title: Regulating young people's access to social media after US court ruling on Meta and Alphabet
asked: Mr Vikram Nair asked whether the Government will consider action to regulate young people's access to social media platforms, including a potential ban, in light of a US court finding that Meta and Alphabet were negligent in designing platforms that harmed young people.
response: Ms Rahayu Mahzam said the harms are real and taken seriously, and that the Government's approach targets specific harms and design features, calibrated by age, which she described as more demanding than a blanket ban. She cited existing measures including the Code of Practice for Online Safety, age assurance for apps, and annual reporting, and said action had been taken against X and TikTok. Moving forward, age assurance will be extended to designated social media services and the focus will go beyond content to design features such as direct messaging from strangers, auto-play, and AI companions. She said the Government is not foreclosing a ban and will take stronger action if needed, while noting that blanket bans are not globally accepted and that Australia has amended its legislation to be more targeted.
